findings.issue_text: **db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25; app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-7,14-17** — The migration copies legacy hosts verbatim using raw SQL, bypassing the model’s normalization. Legacy supported values such as `https://example.com/1234` are therefore stored unchanged, while lookups compare URI host `example.com` to that full stored string. Existing configured hosts stop being allowed after upgrade. Normalize through the model or parse each value to its canonical hostname before inserting, and add a migration test for legacy protocol/path entries.

**app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2,17; db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-6** — Host records have no normalized uniqueness validation or database unique index. Duplicate (including case-variant) host rows can be assigned different categories; `record_for_host(...).first` then chooses an arbitrary mapping. Canonicalize hosts, validate uniqueness case-insensitively, and add a unique index on the canonical value.

**app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:33-39; app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23-25** — Adding a host without choosing a category is allowed and the server assigns Uncategorized, but the success handler immediately sets `host.category` from the still-null `categoryId`. The new row displays without its category and a subsequent edit can fail when accessing `host.category.id`. Initialize `categoryId` to the resolved default or use the saved record’s returned `category_id` before setting the category object.

**app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2,5-7,14-17** — The validation permits a port, but normalization stores `example.com:8080` while `URI(...).host` used in lookup is `example.com`; such a saved host can never authorize embeds. Either strip ports when persisting (matching prior host behavior) or compare a canonical host-and-port consistently.

**app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9-16,22-24; app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-7** — Missing records or a request missing `embeddable_host.host` produce `NoMethodError`/500 responses. Return a 404 for absent IDs and validate/handle missing parameters instead of dereferencing `nil`.

**spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5-7; spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5-7** — New controller tests only assert inheritance. Add behavior tests for CRUD authorization/validation, category assignment, duplicate rejection, and migration preservation of existing settings.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2,17; db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-6** — Host records have no normalized uniqueness validation or database unique index. Duplicate (including case-variant) host rows can be assigned different categories; `record_for_host(...).first` then chooses an arbitrary mapping. Canonicalize hosts, validate uniqueness case-insensitively, and add a unique index on the canonical value.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue. Looking at the diff: 1) EmbeddableHost model (app/models/embeddable_host.rb) has no uniqueness validation on the host field - only a format validation. 2) The migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb) creates the table with just `t.string :host, null: false` but no unique index. 3) The `record_for_host` method uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` which would return an arbitrary record if duplicates exist. 4) The `before_validation` normalizes the host by removing protocol and path, but doesn't prevent case-variant duplicates like 'Example.com' vs 'example.com'. This means duplicate hosts (including case variants) can be inserted with different categories, and the system will arbitrarily pick one when checking permissions. This is a real data integrity and correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:33-39; app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23-25** — Adding a host without choosing a category is allowed and the server assigns Uncategorized, but the success handler immediately sets `host.category` from the still-null `categoryId`. The new row displays without its category and a subsequent edit can fail when accessing `host.category.id`. Initialize `categoryId` to the resolved default or use the saved record’s returned `category_id` before setting the category object.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code flow: In embeddable-host.js.es6, the save() action gets categoryId (line 33) which could be null if user didn't select a category. The server in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23-25 handles this by defaulting to uncategorized_category_id. However, in the success handler (lines 36-38), it does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` using the local categoryId which is still null/undefined, not the server's resolved category_id. This means the category won't be properly set on the client side after save, causing display issues. The finding correctly identifies that the client should use the returned category_id from the server response rather than the potentially-null local categoryId.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2,5-7,14-17** — The validation permits a port, but normalization stores `example.com:8080` while `URI(...).host` used in lookup is `example.com`; such a saved host can never authorize embeds. Either strip ports when persisting (matching prior host behavior) or compare a canonical host-and-port consistently.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the EmbeddableHost model: The validation regex on line 2 allows ports (:[0-9]{1,5}), but the before_validation on lines 5-7 only strips the protocol and path, not the port. So 'example.com:8080' would be stored. In record_for_host (lines 10-17), it uses URI(host).host which returns just 'example.com' without the port. The comparison 'where("lower(host) = ?", host)' would compare 'example.com' against stored 'example.com:8080', which would never match. This is a real bug - hosts saved with ports can never authorize embeds because the lookup strips the port but the stored value retains it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5-7; spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5-7** — New controller tests only assert inheritance. Add behavior tests for CRUD authorization/validation, category assignment, duplicate rejection, and migration preservation of existing settings.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points out that the new controller tests only verify inheritance (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController) without testing actual behavior like CRUD operations, authorization, validation, category assignment, etc. Looking at the diff, the test files at spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb indeed only contain a single test checking inheritance. While the controllers have create, update, destroy actions with authorization (before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff), these behaviors are not tested. However, this is a test coverage concern/suggestion rather than a bug or defect in the actual code. The code itself may work correctly; the finding is about missing tests, which is more of a quality/completeness concern than a real problem with the implementation.
